body: Seems like a similar issue to #582.

So what exactly is the difference between `moduleId` and `moduleName`? Or rather, why are they not the same thing? [The docs](https://github.com/rollup/rollup/wiki/JavaScript-API#moduleid) aren't very elaborate on the subject, they just tell me that the two things exist and UMD apparently uses both. I haven't used AMD before so I'm probably missing something.

Either way it'd probably be a good idea to allow generic moduleNames, regardless of whether or not it's a good idea to actually use them.

Is there really a case for allowing dashes in global names? I'd be in favour of throwing an error if an invalid identifier (or member expression, which probably makes things slightly trickier) is used, since it's almost certainly unintentional, and it's an opportunity to direct people towards the relevant documentation

issue.title: Using a scoped package name break UMD module generation
issue.body:
I want to generate a UMD module where the name is a scoped package, e.g. `@something/modulename`. Doing so triggers an error a build time because the generated code is invalid:

```
factory((global.@something/modulename = {}) ... etc.
```

Would it be possible to detect this kind of situation an instead generate something like:

```
factory((global['@something/modulename'] = {}) ... etc.
```

This is a killer for me because we scope all of our internal modules.

issue.title: Access global.* using array notation
issue.body:
Allow arbitrary `moduleName` (including names with dashes like `ui-router` or scoped npm packages like `@angular/core`) to be added to the global object.

Closes #582
Closes #584
